page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6e-c12g1.12xlarge is an accelerated compute instance within the GPU-optimized family, designed for distributed parallel compute and deep learning workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor, it features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem incorporates 33 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for AVX and AVX-512 extensions.

Hardware acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs delivering a combined total of 128 GB of VRAM (32 GB per GPU). System memory is scaled to match intensive computing requirements, providing 368 GB of host RAM at roughly 7.67 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for data persistence, and operates with a baseline network throughput of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate standard multi-core throughput and memory access speeds relative to its hardware class. The multi-core stress-ng score reaches 35,520.27 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression hits 147.7 GB/sec, placing overall multi-threaded throughput in the middle performance tier. However, single-core processing capabilities reflect the lower base clock of 2.5 GHz, yielding weaker single-threaded results in tests such as gzip compression (19.36 GB/sec) and single-core stress-ng (1,110.4). Memory bandwidth registers at 98.85 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 47.39 GB/sec for writes.

From an efficiency perspective, the instance balances a significant quantity of host memory with four discrete high-memory V100 accelerators. The primary operational tradeoff stems from the absence of bundled local NVMe storage and modest single-threaded performance. Consequently, the ecs.gn6e-c12g1.12xlarge is best suited for multi-GPU model training, parallel inference pipelines, GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics, and large-scale distributed machine learning jobs.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6e-c12g1.12xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server designed for parallel computation and machine learning tasks. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor, it provides 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores) clocked at 2.5 GHz, 368 GB of host memory, and four discrete NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs totaling 128 GB of VRAM. The instance features no bundled local storage, relying on networked block devices alongside a 16 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark metrics highlight solid multi-threaded performance, with multi-core stress-ng achieving 35,520.27 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 147.7 GB/sec, whereas single-core performance remains in the lower tier due to the conservative base clock. The configuration delivers substantial aggregate memory and accelerator density, making it well matched for distributed deep learning, multi-GPU neural network training, computer vision workloads, and scientific computing pipelines.
